entries.title: Recipe used hf_config on PyTorchModel (Olive Studio builder)
entries.root_cause: Older Olive Studio recipes emitted type PyTorchModel with hf_config. Olive 0.13+ PyTorchModelHandler rejects hf_config; Hugging Face sources must use HfModel.
entries.solution: Rebuild the recipe in Olive Studio (Input → Parse & Apply or re-enable passes). Current Studio builders emit HfModel for Hugging Face IDs. If you imported raw JSON, change input_model.type to HfModel and keep model_path as the HF id.

entries.title: Apply Fix or chat Apply did not change pipeline state
entries.root_cause: The diagnostic had no mappable updated_config (applyable=false), or the patch keys are not in Olive Studio's UI mapping (for example data_configs-only remedies).
entries.solution: Follow the Recommended Fix text manually. For calibration data_configs, set Dataset / user script in Input. For chat suggestions, use Apply only when an action card is shown; plain advice has no patch.

entries.title: Olive MCP package missing or mcp 2.x broke FastMCP import
entries.root_cause: Olive Studio's MCP server needs mcp<2 (FastMCP lives under mcp.server.fastmcp in 1.x). Wrong venv or mcp 2.x removes that path.
entries.solution: In olive-mcp-server: pip install -e ".[dev]" "mcp<2". Restart the MCP / app process. Prefer the project .venv used by Olive Studio.

entries.title: Assistant provider not active in Olive Studio
entries.root_cause: Chat/Audit call the server AI runtime. Downloading a local model does not switch Active Provider until Settings saves the provider/model.
entries.solution: Open Assistant → Settings, select the provider (Ollama, OpenRouter, …), pick/load the model, Save. Confirm the sidebar header shows the active provider.

entries.title: Diagnose could not reach Olive MCP tools
entries.root_cause: Olive Studio proxies Diagnose through POST /api/mcp/tool → olive_mcp_server.call_tool. Missing package install, wrong Python, or an unknown tool name yields empty/failed diagnosis.
entries.solution: Install olive-mcp-server into the app .venv (pip install -e olive-mcp-server "mcp<2"). Restart pnpm dev. Re-run Diagnose; you should see title/root_cause from the KB.

entries.title: TensorRT install used a bare version pin
entries.root_cause: Olive Studio Hardware install must pass a package name (for example tensorrt==…) not a lone ==version string.
entries.solution: Use Hardware → Install for TensorRT / TensorRT RTX, or pip install tensorrt==<version> / tensorrt-rtx explicitly in the app .venv. Retry after a successful install.

entries.title: Pulled recipe JSON did not update the pipeline UI
entries.root_cause: Olive Studio GitHub shortcuts and Pull from GitHub load JSON into the Editor tab only. Pipeline toggles change after Parse & Apply.
entries.solution: Open the Editor tab, confirm the JSON, then click Parse & Apply. Shortcuts intentionally do not auto-apply.

entries.title: Isolate Olive Studio cache directory for this experiment
entries.root_cause: Shared cache_dir across experiments can make multi-pass outputs hard to reason about in Studio.
entries.solution: Set a unique cache directory in Infrastructure / workspace settings, then re-run.

entries.title: TensorRT RTX execution provider not registered
entries.root_cause: Consumer TensorRT RTX path needs both the tensorrt-rtx package and a matching ONNX Runtime EP-ABI plugin build, not the full nvinfer TensorRT SDK. Missing install or SM < 7.5 leaves NvTensorRTRTXExecutionProvider unregistered.
entries.solution: Install both tensorrt-rtx and the matching ONNX Runtime EP-ABI plugin (Hardware → Install TensorRT RTX, or pip in the app venv). Requires NVIDIA GPU SM ≥ 7.5 (Turing+). Verify NvTensorRTRTXExecutionProvider appears in onnxruntime.get_available_providers(). Prefer AWQ INT4 (NVModelOpt) over PTQ INT8/QDQ for this EP. Restart the app after install.

entries.title: DirectML execution provider missing or wrong venv
entries.root_cause: DirectML requires Windows 10/11 + DirectX 12 and onnxruntime-directml in the default-family venv. CUDA/GPU ORT wheels do not expose DmlExecutionProvider.
entries.solution: On Windows, install onnxruntime-directml into the Olive Studio default venv (Hardware → DirectML or pip). Do not mix CUDA/TRT packages into the DirectML EP path. Non-Windows hosts cannot run DirectML.

entries.title: WebGPU is browser-only — local Execute Live blocked
entries.root_cause: WebGpuExecutionProvider targets ONNX Runtime Web in the browser. Olive Studio marks WebGPU recipes non-runnable locally (isRunnable: false / localExecutionIssues).
entries.solution: Use Export recipe / download ONNX for in-browser ORT Web WebGPU. Prefer FP16 (OnnxFloatToFloat16). Do not expect Execute Live or local Olive CLI to run WebGPU.

entries.title: OpenVINO NPU needs target device NPU (not EP rename)
entries.root_cause: Intel NPU still uses OpenVINOExecutionProvider. The device is selected separately via openvinoTargetDevice (or equivalent). Without device=NPU and the OpenVINO NPU driver, work stays on CPU.
entries.solution: In Olive Studio set OpenVINO target device to NPU. Install the OpenVINO NPU driver on Intel Core Ultra / Meteor Lake+. Prefer OpenVINO weight-compression or INT8 paths; verify unsupported ops are not silently falling back to CPU.
